card.statement:
Two unicellular linear operators $\cal A$ and $\cal B$ on an $n$-dimensional unitary space are unitarily similar if and only if they have the same eigenvalue and the canonical isomorphism <<ref:hkt>> is isometric $($i.e., it preserves the norm$)$ for each
$k=1,\dots,n$.
card.label: Corollary 2

paper.title: $\phantom{.}$ [-30mm] Criterion of unitary similarity for upper triangular matrices in general position
paper.abstract: Each square complex matrix is unitarily similar to an upper triangular matrix with diagonal entries in any prescribed order. Let A and B be upper triangular n-by-n matrices that (i) are not similar to direct sums of matrices of smaller sizes, or (ii) are in general position and have the same main diagonal. We prove that A and B are unitarily similar if and only if ||h(A_k)||=||h(B_k)|| for all complex polynomials h(x) and k=1, 2, . . , n, where A_k and B_k are the principal k-by-k submatrices of A and B, and ||M|| is the Frobenius norm of M.
